turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
I would prioritize candidates that reproduce the highest-performing motifs in the training set: fullerene-based electron extraction with a hole-blocking interlayer, PTAA or P3CT-type selective hole layers, chemically benign/passivating interlayers, and contacts that do not create strong recombination or extraction barriers.

Top candidates:

1. **c030** — Closest to the very strong training motif `PCBM-60 | Bphen, PTAA | PMMA, Al` that reached ~19.5%. The added IDTT2FPDI/PCBM cascade should maintain good electron extraction and interfacial passivation, while PTAA/PMMA suppresses interfacial recombination and metal-induced damage.

2. **c088** — Very close to the high-performing `C60 | BCP, PTAA, Cu` family, with training examples around 18.6–19.1%. C60/BCP gives selective electron extraction and hole blocking; PTAA is a high-quality hydrophobic hole contact; Cu has worked especially well in this motif.

3. **c097** — Strong analogue of the training row `ITCPTC-Th | C60 | BCP, P3CT-Na, Ag` at ~18.5%. The ITCPTC-Se/C60 cascade plus BCP should reduce recombination, and P3CT-Na is a good selective/passivating hole layer.

4. **c044** — Combines the reliable `PCBM-60 | BCP, PTAA` stack with a Cu back contact. Training data show PTAA/Cu fullerene stacks among the best performers, likely due to good selectivity and reduced contact losses.

5. **c034** — Uses the strong `PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP, PTAA` architecture. Al is somewhat less compelling than Cu here, but the fullerene/BCP cascade and PTAA interface are both associated with high efficiencies in the training data.

Final: c030, c088, c097, c044, c034
